Stewardship & Giving

Ways to give.

The parish is sustained by the regular, prayerful giving of its members. Thank you for considering a gift.

Why we give

A practice, not a transaction.

In the Episcopal tradition, stewardship is not fundraising. It is a spiritual practice. We give because everything we have — our time, our skills, our money, our breath — is a gift, and the proper response to a gift is gratitude. Giving is one of the ways we say thank you with our lives.

The traditional benchmark is the tithe — ten percent of income, with the first portion given to God and the work of the church. Most of us are not there. Most of us are walking toward it. The Episcopal Church asks us to give “the first portion of our income for the spread of the Kingdom of God,” and trusts us to discern what that looks like in our own circumstances. We will never ask you what you make. We will never ask you what you've given. Your pledge is held in confidence by the Treasurer and by no one else.

Below are the ways you can give — one time, monthly, by pledge, by bequest, by directing your IRA, or by giving of yourself in time and skill. All are welcome. None is required.

Monthly

Recurring giving.

The simplest way to give — for both you and the parish — is monthly, automatically. A recurring gift means we can plan, and you don't have to remember.

You can set up a monthly gift through our secure online processor (any amount, any date, easy to change), or by sending us a voided check for a monthly ACH transfer. Many of our members give monthly toward their annual pledge; others give monthly outside the pledge cycle.

Annual stewardship

The 2026 pledge campaign.

Each fall we ask every household to consider a pledge for the coming year — an estimate of giving that lets the vestry build a responsible budget. The campaign begins on the first Sunday of October and culminates in the Ingathering on the first Sunday of Advent, when we bring our pledge cards forward and place them on the altar.

The pledge is a promise of intent, not a contract. It is held in confidence by the Treasurer. Pledges may be adjusted at any time, no questions asked — we have all had years when things changed.

This year's theme: The boat we're all in. The 2026 campaign opens October 4 with a homily from the Rector and a witness from a member of the parish.

Planned giving

The Brendan Society.

The Brendan Society is the parish's planned giving program — the company of those who have included St. Brendan's in their estate plans. It is named for the seafaring saint who, the old story says, set out from an Irish harbor without quite knowing where he would land.

Bequests

A bequest in your will is the simplest planned gift — a percentage of your estate, a specific sum, or the residue after other gifts. Our suggested language: “I give to St. Brendan's Episcopal Church of Kettle Cove, Maine (EIN 01-0556341), [the sum of ___ / ___ percent of the residue of my estate] for its general purposes.”

IRA Qualified Charitable Distributions

If you are 70½ or older, you may direct up to $108,000 (2026 limit) annually from your IRA to the parish without it counting as taxable income. This counts toward your required minimum distribution. Speak with your IRA custodian.

Appreciated securities

Giving long-held stocks, mutual funds, or other appreciated securities lets you avoid capital gains tax and claim a charitable deduction for the full fair-market value. Contact the Treasurer for our brokerage account details.

Charitable gift annuities

Through a relationship with the Episcopal Church Foundation, members can fund a charitable gift annuity that pays you (and a spouse, if desired) a fixed income for life, with the remainder coming to St. Brendan's.

Named funds.

Five named endowment funds were established by members over the past century. Each supports a particular dimension of the parish's life.

The Tasker Music Fund

Established 1957 in memory of Capt. Ezekiel Tasker (founder, 1849). Underwrites the music ministry — choir music, organ maintenance, occasional guest musicians and choral scholars.

Current corpus: $186,000

The Harbor Fund

Established 1894 in memory of three fishermen lost off the Brendan Ledges. Supports the maintenance of the harbor window and the building fabric of the historic church.

Current corpus: $312,000

The Brewster Outreach Fund

Established 2011 by the family of Helen Brewster, a longtime parishioner. Funds the parish's outreach work, with priority to direct relief in our coastal communities.

Current corpus: $94,500

The Bishop Loring Formation Fund

Established 2003 in memory of the Rt. Rev. Chilton R. Loring (Bishop of Maine 1984–1997). Supports children's and adult Christian formation programs, including Vacation Bible School.

Current corpus: $68,200

The Rector's Discretionary Fund

A confidential fund administered solely by the Rector for pastoral need — rent in a hard month, a utility bill, a tank of heating oil. Replenished annually by Easter and Christmas offerings.

Replenished annually

Beyond money

Time. Talent. Treasure.

The old stewardship language speaks of three things, and means it. Money is one part — an important part — of how we offer our lives to God and to one another. It is not the only part.

Time. Showing up matters. Coming on Sunday is not just for you; it is for the person who walks in for the first time and finds the pews already half full. Coming Wednesday at noon to the Healing Eucharist is a gift to the person who sat at home wondering whether anyone would be there. Showing up is a form of giving.

Talent. You can read. Or sing. Or count. Or cook. Or sit quietly with someone who is grieving. Or fix a leaky valve. Every one of those is a need this parish has, right now. See the ministries page, or speak with the Rector.

Treasure. Of course. The lights have to stay on; the curate has to be paid; the food bank's pallet has to be filled. Give what you can. If you can't right now, please come anyway. The table is not behind a paywall.

For your records

Tax information.

St. Brendan's Episcopal Church of Kettle Cove, Maine is a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt religious organization. All gifts are deductible as charitable contributions to the full extent permitted by law.

Legal name: St. Brendan's Episcopal Church of Kettle Cove, Maine
EIN: 01-0556341
Address: 47 Harbor Road, Kettle Cove, ME 04062
Diocese: The Episcopal Diocese of Maine (Province I)

Annual statements of giving are mailed to all donors by January 31. If you need a statement at any other time, please email treasurer@stbrendanskettlecove.org.

We are not in a position to give individual tax or financial advice. Please consult your own advisor on matters of estate planning, qualified charitable distributions, or appreciated-securities gifts.
